judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard definition of the Specifications by content; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.4 identifies no Specifications and points to a Project Manual dated 'n/a', so the defined term has no identified referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Project Manual permissively ('may include'); definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.3 records the Project Manual as 'n/a'/TBD while 15.1.4 incorporates Specifications 'contained in the Project Manual,' leaving the incorporation empty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Complementary' documents and performance limited to what is 'reasonably inferable ... as being necessary to produce the indicated results' is the central interpretive standard of the form and is inherently elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 resolves inconsistencies in favour of the better quality or more stringent requirement, while Agreement Article 1 resolves them in favour of the Agreement and 5.2.6 addresses further development—three different rules for the same problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short rule about the organisation of the Specifications; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement 10.1 on subcontracting; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It adopts 'well-known technical or construction industry meanings,' a standard that invites extrinsic evidence about trade usage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.3.1 and 1.4.1; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical rule about capitalised terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the defined-term scheme in 1.1; nothing conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An interpretive canon that expressly concedes modifiers such as 'all' and 'any' have been omitted, which is itself a licence to argue about scope in particular clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies across A201 but does not contradict any specific provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple execution requirement with an identification mechanism for unsigned documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several enumerated Contract Documents here (the exhibits, and the signature blocks of the Addendum and Supplementary Conditions) are undated or unsigned, so the identification mechanism matters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short deemed representation on execution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Addendum 14.6(d)'s site-visit warranty and sits alongside A201 4.3.4's claim right for concealed conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully drafted intellectual-property clause with express carve-outs; length is not ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.1.1 and 2.2.5; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription is fragmentary, but the obligation—furnish record legal title information on request—is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports the lien machinery in A201 4.4.8 and Addendum 12.1.4(b); nothing inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made' is undefined, yet furnishing it is made 'a condition precedent to commencement or continuation of the Work.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 14.1.1.4 lets the Contractor terminate for failure to furnish this evidence, and Agreement 4.1/4.3 fix commencement and completion dates that a suspension for lack of evidence would disturb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates easements, assessments and charges to the Owner with an express carve-out for 3.7.1 permits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit and inspection fees a reimbursable Cost of the Work, so the allocation is economically the Owner's either way; no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Owner-furnished surveys and legal description with a reliance right; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads with 2.1.2 and 4.3.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' is a soft timing standard, but a familiar one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Agreement Article 3's Owner covenant to furnish information in a timely manner.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such copies ... as are reasonably necessary' is elastic but minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.4 makes document reproduction a reimbursable cost, which overlaps the 'free of charge' provision here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stop-work right with an express disclaimer of any duty to exercise it; clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 2.4.1 and 12.2; Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds the Owner to Architect approvals but does not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-notice cure procedure with a defined Change Order remedy; internally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.4.1 [Revision] deletes the second notice and shortens the procedure, while the Supplementary Conditions preamble says unaltered General Conditions provisions remain in effect—so two cure regimes coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agreement's identification of the Contractor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line performance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Agreement Article 2 and its Addendum revision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A non-waiver provision in standard terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.3 and 9.6.6; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause simultaneously requires careful study and disclaims that the review is 'for the purpose of discovering errors, omissions, or inconsistencies,' a tension litigants regularly exploit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for the correctness of field measurements with 'no extra charge,' and 1.2.1.1 requires the more stringent requirement, which cuts against the limited-purpose disclaimer here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Distinguishes the Contractor's contractor-capacity review from design responsibility; the boundary is stated but inherently blurry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires shop drawings prepared by trade experts and, where required, a licensed engineer, edging the Contractor toward design responsibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Preserves claims for cost or time from clarifications while imposing damages for failure to report; the two limbs are dense but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 permits increases only by Change Order and bars unjust-enrichment claims, and 1.2.1.1(b) allows 'no extra charge' for dimensional differences; the claim right here must be squared with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The warranty exclusions—'improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage'—are evaluative and frequently litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In this cost-plus contract 7.7.3 makes the cost of correcting non-negligent nonconforming Work reimbursable, so who pays for warranty correction is not settled by the warranty alone; 12.2.2 supplies the correction period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short tax-payment obligation keyed to taxes enacted or effective when bids are received or negotiations concluded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.2 makes sales, use and similar taxes a reimbursable Cost of the Work and Exhibit D treats the Hawaii general excise tax as a job cost calculated on direct costs, so the Contractor 'pays' but the Owner funds—two different allocations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customarily secured after execution of the Contract' and 'legally required when bids are received or negotiations concluded' are timing qualifiers that could be argued but are standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees reimbursable, and revised 4.1 makes commencement itself 'pending approval of permits,' so permit responsibility and timing are addressed in three places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general compliance obligation, plainly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7.3, 3.7.4 and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Disclaims a duty to ascertain legal conformity but imposes a duty to report observed variances—an interplay that is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 requires compliance with the more stringent of the documents and applicable codes, which presses beyond mere reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowing it to be contrary' sets a scienter test; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with 3.7.3 and with 8.1.6's exclusion of costs due to the Contractor's failure to fulfil responsibilities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward requirement to include stated allowances in the Contract Sum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.4 states no allowances and the Contract Sum here is Cost of the Work plus Fee rather than a fixed price, so the allowance machinery has little to bite on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three-part allocation between allowance amounts and Contract Sum items is detailed, though the line between 'costs' and 'other expenses contemplated' can be argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes a fixed Contract Sum adjusted by Change Order, whereas Agreement 5.1.1 and Article 7 reimburse actual Cost of the Work; with no allowances stated in 5.2.4 the mechanism is orphaned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A timing obligation on the Owner; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on allowances that 5.2.4 never states.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Competent superintendent and necessary assistants' is qualitative but conventional, and the binding-communications rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum Article 2 [Revised] requires designation of one supervisory employee responsible for the project, and 7.2.2 makes site supervisory salaries reimbursable only with Owner approval—three overlapping requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A submittal-schedule requirement; unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 and A201 4.2.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In general accordance with the most recent schedules' is a deliberately loose performance standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.10.4 makes the Construction Schedule part of the Contract Documents with monitoring and updating duties, which is a stricter regime than 'general accordance.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A record-keeping requirement listing the documents to be maintained; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Agreement Article 11 accounting records and A201 9.10.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.12.4 and Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; 'standards by which the Work will be judged' is standard AIA language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.5 warranty and 4.2.7 review limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States plainly that submittals are not Contract Documents and explains their purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 deem the Construction Schedule and cost estimates to be Contract Documents, so the instrument treats contractor-generated documents inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Review-approve-submit sequence with a promptness standard; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.7 and Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or will do so' softens the representation slightly, but the obligation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads with 3.12.5 and 3.12.8; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two numbered escape routes from the deviation rule are precise, though the clause is dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 requires a Change Order for any change in Contract Sum or Time, which matches limb (2) here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific notice rule with a stated consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.12.8; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The boundary between services the Contract Documents 'specifically require' and services needed for means and methods is the sort of line that generates design-responsibility disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires shop drawings by a licensed engineer 'if required by the Architect or the Owner or applicable law,' which enlarges the Contractor's design role beyond what this paragraph contemplates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably encumber the site' is a soft standard but a minor one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.15 cleaning up and 10.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short responsibility allocation for cutting and patching.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads with 6.2.5 and 7.5.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably withhold' consent appears twice with reciprocal effect; the drafting is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Article 6 on separate contractors; no separate contracts are identified here, which limits its operation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line access obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 11 audit rights and A201 4.2.2.
